questions.question: Which of the following are the components of Von-Neumann architecture?

options.text: Hard disks, floppy disks and CPU

questions.answer: **Correct answer: D) Memory, input/output modules and CPU.**

questions.question: Which of the following computer memory is fastest?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) register.** Registers sit at the top of the memory hierarchy.

questions.question: In the parity generator which logic operator is used to generate the parity bit?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: D) XOR.** XOR of all data bits gives even parity.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic of RISC?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) Large instruction set.** RISC uses a small, simple instruction set.

questions.question: What is computer organization?

options.text: structure and behavior of a computer system as observed by the user
structure of a computer system as observed by the developer
structure and behavior of a computer system as observed by the developer

questions.answer: **Correct answer: C.** Computer organization concerns the operational units and interconnections visible to a system designer.

questions.question: The content of an 8-bit register is initially `10011100`, what is the content after a shift-right operation?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) 01001110.** A logical shift right inserts 0 at the left.

questions.question: The performance of cache memory is frequently measured in terms of ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) hit ratio.**

questions.question: Both the CISC and RISC architectures have been developed to reduce the ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) Semantic gap.** Both aim to bridge the gap between high-level languages and machine instructions (in different ways).

questions.question: Which are the different type/s of generating control signals?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: D) Both Micro-programmed and Hardwired.**

questions.question: The small extremely fast RAMs are called as ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: D) Cache.**

questions.question: MAR stands for ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) Memory Address Register.**

questions.question: In order to read multiple bytes of a row at the same time, we make use of ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) Memory extension.** Wider memory organization reads multiple bytes in one access.

questions.question: Cache memory uses ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) SRAM.** Static RAM is faster and does not need refresh.

questions.question: Computer address bus is ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: C) Unidirectional.** The CPU drives addresses to memory/I/O.

questions.question: The address in the main memory is known as ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) Physical address.**

questions.question: Full form of RISC is ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) Reduced instruction set computer.**

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is(are) true?

options.text: PC points to the next instruction to be executed
Stack works on the principle of FIFO

questions.answer: **Model answer: D; statement B is also true.** ROM is read-only, the program counter points to the next instruction, a stack is LIFO (not FIFO), and RAM is read/write. The scan offers no “B and D” combination option, so D is retained as the single-letter practice key.

questions.question: DMA stands for ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: C) Direct memory access.**

questions.question: What is the full form of MBR?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) memory buffer register.**

questions.question: IEEE double precision format is ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: D) 64 bits.** Single precision is 32 bits; double precision is 64 bits.

questions.question: Full form of PC is ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: C) program counter.**

questions.question: Theoretically maximum speedup that a pipeline can provide depends on the ______.

options.text: number of segments on the pipeline

questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) number of segments on the pipeline.** Ideal speedup approaches the number of stages.

questions.question: Which memory is difficult to interface with processor?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) Dynamic memory.** DRAM needs refresh and multiplexed address timing.

questions.question: An example of direct addressing mode is ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) LDA 2021H.** `MOV C,B` is register addressing.

questions.question: Which mode of DMA is fastest?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) burst mode.** The DMA controller owns the bus for the whole block transfer.

b) Explain the function of BIU & EU.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Write the restoring division process with flowchart and example.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Explain the function of BIU & EU.

questions.answer:
**a)** Initialize remainder R=0; for each dividend bit: shift R left with next bit, subtract divisor, if negative restore R and set quotient bit 0, else set 1. Example 7 ÷ 3 gives quotient 2, remainder 1.

**b)** 8086 BIU fetches instructions, manages the queue and buses; EU decodes/executes instructions using ALU and registers.

questions.question:
a) What do you mean by hit and miss ratio?
b) A typical computer system cache memory access time is 8 ns and its main memory access time is 65 ns. If hit ratio is 90%, what is the average memory access time?

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: What do you mean by hit and miss ratio?

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: A typical computer system cache memory access time is 8 ns and its main memory access time is 65 ns. If hit ratio is 90%, what is the average memory access time?

questions.answer:
**Mark distribution — Total 8 marks: a) 2 marks (definitions) + b) 6 marks (calculation).**

**a) Hit ratio and Miss ratio**

- **Hit ratio (h)**: the fraction of memory accesses that are found in the cache.
  `Hit ratio = (number of hits) / (total number of memory accesses)`
- **Miss ratio**: the fraction of accesses not found in cache (must go to main memory).
  `Miss ratio = 1 − Hit ratio = (number of misses) / (total accesses)`

If hit ratio is 90% (h = 0.9), miss ratio is 10% (0.1).

**b) Average memory access time**

Given:
- Cache access time `Tc = 8 ns`
- Main memory access time `Tm = 65 ns`
- Hit ratio `h = 90% = 0.9`, so miss ratio = 0.1

When there is a hit, time = `Tc`.
When there is a miss, the cache is checked first (8 ns) and then main memory (65 ns), so miss time = `Tc + Tm = 8 + 65 = 73 ns`.

Average access time:
```
Tavg = h × Tc + (1 − h) × (Tc + Tm)
     = 0.9 × 8 + 0.1 × (8 + 65)
     = 7.2 + 0.1 × 73
     = 7.2 + 7.3
     = 14.5 ns
```

**Average memory access time = 14.5 ns.**

(If the convention used ignores re-accessing cache on a miss, then `Tavg = h·Tc + (1−h)·Tm = 7.2 + 6.5 = 13.7 ns`; the standard inclusive formula gives 14.5 ns.)

questions.question:
a) What do you mean by cache memory mapping?
b) Write down the direct cache memory mapping technique and what is its main disadvantage.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: What do you mean by cache memory mapping?

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Write down the direct cache memory mapping technique and what is its main disadvantage.

questions.answer:
**a)** Mapping decides where a main-memory block may reside in cache.

**b)** Direct mapping: cache line = (memory block number) mod (number of cache lines); tag stores the rest. Main disadvantage: conflict misses even when cache has free lines elsewhere.

questions.question:
a) Write the different pipeline hazards.
b) Explain the different groups of computers according to Flynn’s classification.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Explain the different groups of computers according to Flynn’s classification.

questions.answer:
**Mark distribution — Total 8 marks: a) 4 marks (hazards) + b) 4 marks (Flynn's classification).**

**a) Pipeline hazards**

In a pipelined processor, multiple instructions overlap in execution. A **hazard** is a situation that prevents the next instruction from executing in its scheduled clock cycle, reducing performance. There are three types:

1. **Structural hazard**: two instructions need the same hardware resource at the same time (e.g. a single memory used for both instruction fetch and data access). Resolved by duplicating resources or stalling.
2. **Data hazard**: an instruction depends on the result of a previous instruction still in the pipeline.
   - **RAW (Read After Write)**: true dependency — instruction needs a value not yet produced.
   - **WAR (Write After Read)**: anti-dependency — instruction writes a value before a previous one reads it.
   - **WAW (Write After Write)**: output dependency — two instructions write the same location.
   Resolved by forwarding (bypassing) or pipeline stalls.
3. **Control (branch) hazard**: caused by branch instructions — the processor does not know the next instruction address until the branch is resolved. Resolved by branch prediction, delayed branches, or flushing the pipeline.

**b) Flynn's classification of computers**

M. J. Flynn classified computers based on the number of instruction streams and data streams processed simultaneously:

| Class | Instruction stream | Data stream | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SISD** | Single | Single | One CPU executes one instruction stream on one data stream. | Traditional uniprocessor PC |
| **SIMD** | Single | Multiple | One instruction operates on multiple data items simultaneously. | Vector processors, GPU arrays |
| **MISD** | Multiple | Single | Multiple instructions operate on a single data stream. | Rare; systolic arrays, fault-tolerant systems |
| **MIMD** | Multiple | Multiple | Multiple processors execute different instructions on different data. | Multi-core CPUs, clusters, servers |

Most modern computers (multi-core PCs, servers) are **MIMD**, while graphics units use **SIMD**.

questions.question:
a) Draw the pin diagram of 8086 microprocessor.
b) Explain maximum and minimum mode of 8086 microprocessor.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Draw the pin diagram of 8086 microprocessor.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Explain maximum and minimum mode of 8086 microprocessor.

questions.answer:
**a)** 40-pin DIP: multiplexed AD0–AD15, A16/S3–A19/S6, `BHE/S7`, `RD`, `READY`, `RESET`, `CLK`, `MN/MX`, `VCC`/GND, interrupt and DMA/control pins; pin functions differ by mode.

**b)** Minimum mode (`MN/MX=1`): single processor, 8086 generates control signals. Maximum mode (`MN/MX=0`): multiprocessor/coprocessor system, 8288 bus controller generates commands.

questions.question: a) Write short notes on any two: (i) TLB (ii) DMA (iii) Virtual Memory.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Write short notes on any two: (i) TLB (ii) DMA (iii) Virtual Memory.

questions.answer:
**TLB:** cache of recent virtual-to-physical page translations.

**DMA:** peripheral transfers a block to/from memory without CPU byte-by-byte involvement.

**Virtual Memory:** gives each process a large logical address space by paging/swapping between RAM and secondary storage.

questions.question:
a) What do you mean by micro operation?
b) Explain the functioning procedure of micro-programmed control unit.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: What do you mean by micro operation?

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Explain the functioning procedure of micro-programmed control unit.

questions.answer:
**a)** A micro-operation is an elementary register-transfer step, e.g. `PC ← PC + 1`.

**b)** Instruction opcode maps to a microprogram in control store; a micro-PC sequences microinstructions whose fields emit control signals and branch/condition bits until the machine instruction completes.
